subject: How to avoid growth() crashing the entire program?

messages.author: 4d08b8c7e2e8742d
messages.subject: How to avoid growth() crashing the entire program?
parts:
I am sure this has been discussed so I would be obliged if someone pointed me at  an earlier discussion. I was not clear how to search for this.

Bottom line: growth() can abort and I want my program to continue.

I am running growth() on many data files in a program loop. Until now, all runs of growth have returned a lavaan object even when it did not converge but if the name of the returned object was "fit" I could get the status as fit@Fit@converged and then not call fitmeasures() as it aborted badly if fed such a fit so it throws one..

But now growth() itself aborted with an enigmatic error:

Error in chol.default(S) : 
  the leading minor of order 2 is not positive definite

I am expecting many of the data files not to converge and that is fine. But I want all my files to be run and the script to continue to other things.

So choice one is to ask if the lavaan family has a way to tell it to abort more gently. There seem to be hundreds of such options, many of which sound mysterious. I would be happy if it exited with a return value of NULL or an empty object or something.

Choice two is to ask R to protect me with something like trycatch() . The idea would be to wrap each of several calls to growth with different models in such a call and on error, set a boolean variable to signal there was an error so I do not try to get assorted statistics out of the fit and just set my results to NA and move on.

Yes, in case you wonder, my data deliberately is such that I expect many of the examples to fail for one model or another as some of it is partially random. There will be matrices that are not invertable or other glitches and that is fine with me as long as I can continue merrily along to the end and have data I can slice and dice.

If there is no current option, who would be asked about adding something like abort_pos_def=FALSE or perhaps telling them to return a minus one as in abort=-1 as often happens in other languages and environments?

To recap, I am happy with what lavaan offers but want it to NOT blow things up. An example of how others have done it would be appreciated.

messages.author: 4d08b8c7e2e8742d
messages.subject: Re: How to avoid growth() crashing the entire program?
parts:
While waiting to see if anyone had a better answer, I decided to try shielding my code like this:

fit <-  tryCatch({
  growth(model, data = mine)
},
error = function(cond) {
  return(NULL)
})

I chose to not do anything for warnings as I handle the main one.

Then I decide what to do after it returns by checking:

if (is.null(fit)) {
   # Record failure and continue 
} else {
  # code already there on success and continue
}

It does complicate matters as I now save whether it tried to crash as a column in my data.frame as well as columns for convergence and number of iterations and assorted stats I mine from the fit, when it is not NULL.

I will know by morning if this runs to completion as it is s l o w .

Then I get to make more complicated queries that handle several causes of failure.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: How to avoid growth() crashing the entire program?
parts:
On 6/5/20 1:03 AM, SpocK KirK wrote:
> Bottom line: growth() can abort and I want my program to continue.

In a simulation, I always use try() to handle any 'fatal' exceptions.

> the status as fit@Fit@converged

Better use

lavInspect(fit, "converged")

which returns TRUE or FALSE.

> But now growth() itself aborted with an enigmatic error:
>

> /Error in chol.default(S) : /
> /  the leading minor of order 2 is not positive definite/

Hm. That is not supposed to happend. Could you email me the datafile
(and script) that caused this? lavaan tries hard to 'catch' non-positive
definite matrices before we call chol(), but this one slipped through.
The end result would still be a fatal error, but at least with a more
informative message.

> So choice one is to ask if the lavaan family has a way to tell it to
> abort more gently. There seem to be hundreds of such options, many of
> which sound mysterious. I would be happy if it exited with a return
> value of NULL or an empty object or something.

I see your point, this will never be fully bullet proof. A hard stop
(with an error message) is often necessary. And in R, we have plenty of
error recovery functionality, eg try().

> Choice two is to ask R to protect me with something like trycatch() .
> The idea would be to wrap each of several calls to growth with different
> models in such a call and on error, set a boolean variable to signal
> there was an error so I do not try to get assorted statistics out of the
> fit and just set my results to NA and move on.

That is a very common approach.

Yves.

messages.author: 4d08b8c7e2e8742d
messages.subject: Re: How to avoid growth() crashing the entire program?
parts:
Thank you, Yves.

My version of "R caution" worked fine and let my script on Windows continue to the end. I did take your advice and am using lavInspect(fit, "converged") rather than the simpler method I adopted of peeking directly into the fit. Just FYI, both show a TRUE/FALSE answer. I assume as lavaan keeps being developed, I cannot rely on the internals being the same, albeit the tools presumably will remain working.

If you really would like the file that caused this discussion, I can send it to you privately.
